name: Banjara Gosht
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadhai until smoking, then temper with cumin, cinnamon, cloves, cardamoms, and dried red chilies.
2. Add the sliced onions and sauté until they turn golden brown.
3. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
4. Add the mutton pieces and sear on high heat until browned.
5. Lower the heat, whisk in the yogurt, and add turmeric, coriander powder, chili powder, and salt.
6. Cover and cook on low heat (dum style) adding minimal water until the meat is succulent and tender.
7. Finish with garam masala and garnish with fresh coriander.
description: Banjara Gosht is a signature dish of the Banjara tribe of Rajasthan, known for their nomadic lifestyle. The recipe was designed to be prepared in camp-style settings with easily portable spices, resulting in a robust, pungent, and deeply aromatic curry that showcases the intense flavor profiles of Rajasthani cuisine.
